Confirmed: item 5 lacks the smoothness/lissity hypotheses needed for its ordinary-cohomology lower bound. A split irreducible nodal proper rational curve over a finite field with the constant pure weight-zero sheaf has H¹ of weight zero. Correct the formulation: compact-support upper bounds for separated finite-type mixed sheaves of weights ≤w; ordinary lower bounds for a smooth variety and lisse pure weight-w coefficients; then purity of the image H_c→H. State the local boundary estimate on the appropriate smooth complete curve, rather than claiming the same lower bound on every singular X.

Confirmed from the displayed local equations on pp. 41 and 45 and the claimed model on the rendered p. 50. At a nonzero orbit index a or b, c=2ap or 2bp and e=v_p(c)=1+v_p(a) or 1+v_p(b). After adjoining π=√(-p), the form is Q-uπ^(2e), not always Q-uπ² with u a unit. For k=9,p=3,a=3, c=18=2π⁴; in the π-chart after one blow-up the strict transform still has a quadratic-cone special fiber and a singular vertex. The analogous example k=18,p=3,b=6 has the same excess thickness. Record a proof gap affecting Proposition 5.23 and the dependent Corollary 5.27 argument for these small-prime cases. The e=1 argument remains separate. Require a verified iterated-resolution/comparison argument or a separately proved replacement; do not assert that Remark 5.41 alone supplies the missing rigid-to-de Rham comparison or Newton inequality. I have not independently obtained Mieda's paper and do not certify its hypotheses or the proposed repair.
